note: Seed set written by hand. Replace and extend with real learner utterances before trusting any number.

scene.relationship: their manager
scene.situation: The manager is asking the learner to take on extra work this week.

cases.learner_message: I can't take that on this week. I'm at capacity until Friday.
cases.why: Direct and complete: reason plus limit. Fine with a manager.

scene.relationship: their manager
scene.situation: The manager is asking the learner to take on extra work this week.

cases.learner_message: I don't agree. The numbers don't support it.
cases.why: A plain, reasoned disagreement is normal at work.

scene.relationship: a coworker they get along with
scene.situation: Two coworkers chatting at the next desks about the day.

cases.learner_message: Can you cover my shift Friday? I'll take yours Sunday.
cases.why: A direct request that offers something back.

scene.relationship: a coworker they get along with
scene.situation: Two coworkers chatting at the next desks about the day.

cases.learner_message: I'd love to, but I can't this week.
cases.why: Ordinary, proportionate softening.

scene.relationship: a close friend
scene.situation: Two friends making weekend plans over text.

cases.learner_message: Sure. Tomorrow works. Seven?
cases.why: Short and fluent; no discourse markers is not a defect.

scene.relationship: a close friend
scene.situation: Two friends making weekend plans over text.

cases.learner_message: Yeah, I'll grab the tickets.
cases.why: Complete, natural, brief.

scene.relationship: a coworker they get along with
scene.situation: Two coworkers chatting at the next desks about the day.

cases.learner_message: Long day. You?
cases.why: Fragments and ellipsis are normal speech.

scene.relationship: a coworker they get along with
scene.situation: Two coworkers chatting at the next desks about the day.

cases.learner_message: I was going to - well, I thought we could, you know, start at nine.
cases.why: A normal restart with fillers.

scene.relationship: a close friend
scene.situation: Two friends making weekend plans over text.

cases.learner_message: Dude, that's insane. I'm so down.
cases.why: Slang that fits friends texting.

scene.relationship: a coworker they get along with
scene.situation: Two coworkers chatting at the next desks about the day.

cases.learner_message: I'm literally dying, this line is taking forever.
cases.why: Idiomatic hyperbole between friendly coworkers.

scene.relationship: a senior stakeholder
scene.situation: A formal review with a senior stakeholder.

cases.learner_message: I would suggest that we revisit the timeline before committing to a date.
cases.why: Formal wording in a formal scene.

scene.relationship: a colleague in a project meeting
scene.situation: A planning meeting about a product launch timeline.

cases.learner_message: One could argue that the timeline is optimistic.
cases.why: Slightly formal, fully natural in a meeting.

scene.relationship: a close friend
scene.situation: Two friends making weekend plans over text.

cases.learner_message: I'd rather not, if it's all the same to you.
cases.why: Correct and a little formal; a native would not react.

scene.relationship: a close friend
scene.situation: Two friends making weekend plans over text.

cases.learner_message: I'll ring you at the weekend.
cases.why: British variety, natural English.

scene.relationship: a coworker they get along with
scene.situation: Two coworkers chatting at the next desks about the day.

cases.learner_message: She's gotten really good at it.
cases.why: Standard American usage.

scene.relationship: a close friend
scene.situation: Two friends making weekend plans over text.

cases.learner_message: Who are you going with?
cases.why: Sentence-final preposition and 'who' are normal speech.

scene.relationship: a coworker they get along with
scene.situation: Two coworkers chatting at the next desks about the day.

cases.learner_message: Someone left their jacket here. They'll want it back.
cases.why: Singular 'they' is standard.

scene.relationship: a coworker they get along with
scene.situation: Two coworkers chatting at the next desks about the day.

cases.learner_message: I'm gonna grab a coffee, you want one?
cases.why: Spoken reductions are natural here.

scene.relationship: a client
scene.situation: A call with a client about a delayed delivery.

cases.learner_message: I'm really sorry to bring this up, but I think we might miss the deadline. Could we talk about options?
cases.why: Bad news to a client: heavy cushioning is right.

scene.relationship: a coworker they get along with
scene.situation: Two coworkers chatting at the next desks about the day.

cases.learner_message: Could you send me the file, please?
cases.why: One 'could you' and one 'please' is ordinary politeness.

scene.relationship: a close friend
scene.situation: Two friends making weekend plans over text.

cases.learner_message: God willing, I'll see you Friday.
cases.why: A formula the learner chose; not an error.

scene.relationship: a coworker they get along with
scene.situation: Two coworkers chatting at the next desks about the day.

cases.learner_message: yeah i think thats right we should probably move it to thursday
cases.why: Lowercase and no punctuation are transcription artifacts.

scene.relationship: a colleague in a project meeting
scene.situation: A planning meeting about a product launch timeline.

cases.learner_message: I need to take a decision by Friday.
cases.why: English says make a decision.

scene.relationship: a coworker they get along with
scene.situation: Two coworkers chatting at the next desks about the day.

cases.learner_message: I have many works to finish today.
cases.why: 'Work' (tasks) is uncountable.

scene.relationship: their manager
scene.situation: The manager is asking the learner to take on extra work this week.

cases.learner_message: No. I can't do it.
cases.why: To a manager a refusal with no reason and no way forward is curt.

scene.relationship: a coworker they get along with
scene.situation: Two coworkers chatting at the next desks about the day.

cases.learner_message: Excuse me, sorry, if you don't mind, if it's possible, could you maybe possibly send me the file, please?

findings.span: if you don't mind, if it's possible, could you maybe possibly

cases.why: Politeness stacked until the request is lost.

scene.relationship: a close friend
scene.situation: Two friends making weekend plans over text.

cases.learner_message: Moreover, I would like to inform you that I am hungry.
cases.why: Written connector and stiff phrasing in a casual chat.

scene.relationship: a coworker they get along with
scene.situation: Two coworkers chatting at the next desks about the day.

cases.learner_message: Please be informed that the meeting is moved to Thursday.
cases.why: Bureaucratic opener between peers.

scene.relationship: a coworker they get along with
scene.situation: Two coworkers chatting at the next desks about the day.

cases.learner_message: Hello my friend, can you send me the report?
cases.why: 'My friend' to a coworker can sound patronising.

scene.relationship: a close friend
scene.situation: Two friends making weekend plans over text.

cases.learner_message: I will make a party tomorrow.
cases.why: English says throw or have a party.

scene.relationship: a colleague in a project meeting
scene.situation: A planning meeting about a product launch timeline.

cases.learner_message: I'm agree with you.
cases.why: 'Agree' is a verb, not an adjective: I agree.

scene.relationship: a coworker they get along with
scene.situation: Two coworkers chatting at the next desks about the day.

cases.learner_message: She said me that she was busy.
cases.why: She told me / she said that.

scene.relationship: a coworker they get along with
scene.situation: Two coworkers chatting at the next desks about the day.

cases.learner_message: I have meeting at three.
cases.why: Article missing: I have a meeting.

scene.relationship: a coworker they get along with
scene.situation: Two coworkers chatting at the next desks about the day.

cases.learner_message: Yesterday I lost the bus and so I was late for the meeting then angry the boss.
cases.why: A listener would not know who was angry at whom.

scene.relationship: a colleague in a project meeting
scene.situation: A planning meeting about a product launch timeline.

cases.learner_message: I swear to God this is the worst meeting in the history of the world, I will die.
cases.why: Over-intense for a work meeting.
